description: CloudFront Origin buckets must enforce access restriction

requirements.description: CloudFront Distribution has an S3 origin (S3OriginConfig present) with neither OriginAccessIdentity (empty/absent) nor OriginAccessControlId set
requirements.rationale: AWS documentation requires restricting S3 origin access via either OAI (legacy) or OAC. With both absent, the S3 bucket is directly reachable, violating the rule.

requirements.description: CloudFront Distribution has an S3 origin where S3OriginConfig.OriginAccessIdentity is set to a non-empty OAI value (e.g., 'origin-access-identity/cloudfront/E1XXXXXX') and no OriginAccessControlId
requirements.rationale: A non-empty OriginAccessIdentity restricts S3 access through CloudFront only. This is the legacy-but-valid compliance path per AWS documentation.

requirements.description: CloudFront Distribution has an S3 origin where OriginAccessControlId is set (referring to an AWS::CloudFront::OriginAccessControl) and S3OriginConfig.OriginAccessIdentity is empty
requirements.rationale: OAC is the AWS-recommended mechanism for restricting S3 origin access. Per docs, when using OAC, OriginAccessIdentity should be empty. This satisfies the rule.

requirements.description: CloudFront Distribution has an S3 origin with S3OriginConfig.OriginAccessIdentity present but explicitly set to empty string and no OriginAccessControlId
requirements.rationale: An empty OriginAccessIdentity (per AWS docs) means viewers can access objects via the S3 URL directly, effectively disabling restriction. Without OAC also, no restriction is enforced.

requirements.description: CloudFront Distribution origin uses CustomOriginConfig pointing to an S3 website endpoint (not S3OriginConfig)
requirements.rationale: S3 website endpoints must use CustomOriginConfig and cannot use OAI/OAC per AWS docs. The rule targets S3OriginConfig origins; website-endpoint S3 origins are out of scope (resolved decision).

requirements.description: CloudFront Distribution has multiple origins where at least one S3 origin lacks both OAI and OAC, while another S3 origin has OAC configured
requirements.rationale: Each S3 origin must independently enforce restriction. Even one unrestricted S3 origin in the distribution is non-compliant.

requirements.description: CloudFront Distribution has multiple S3 origins where every S3 origin has either OAI or OAC properly configured
requirements.rationale: All S3 origins enforce access restriction via a valid mechanism (OAI or OAC). Rule is satisfied.

requirements.description: CloudFront Distribution Origins property is an empty array
requirements.rationale: With no origins defined, there are no S3 origin buckets to enforce access restriction on. The rule has nothing to evaluate.

requirements.description: CloudFront Distribution S3 origin's OriginAccessControlId is provided as an unresolvable intrinsic function (Fn::ImportValue or Fn::If with unknowable conditions)
requirements.rationale: When the OAC reference cannot be resolved at scan time, the rule cannot definitively assert non-compliance and should not flag a false positive.

requirements.description: CloudFront Distribution S3 origin's OriginAccessIdentity value is an unresolvable intrinsic function (e.g., Fn::ImportValue)
requirements.rationale: When the OAI value cannot be resolved at scan time, the rule cannot prove the value is empty/non-compliant and should pass to avoid false positives.

requirements.description: CloudFront Distribution S3 origin uses Fn::GetAtt or Ref to reference an AWS::CloudFront::CloudFrontOriginAccessIdentity resource for OriginAccessIdentity
requirements.rationale: Per evaluation model, Fn::GetAtt/Ref resolve to the logical ID of the referenced OAI resource. This is a valid configured restriction and the rule should pass.

requirements.description: CloudFront Distribution S3 origin uses Ref to reference an AWS::CloudFront::OriginAccessControl resource for OriginAccessControlId
requirements.rationale: Ref to an OAC resource resolves to its logical ID, indicating OAC is configured for the origin. This satisfies the rule.

requirements.description: CloudFront Distribution origin has VpcOriginConfig (VPC origin) and not S3OriginConfig
requirements.rationale: VPC origins are not S3 buckets. The rule targets S3 origin buckets; VPC origins are outside the rule's scope.

requirements.description: CloudFront Distribution S3 origin has both OriginAccessIdentity (non-empty) and OriginAccessControlId set
requirements.rationale: At least one valid restriction mechanism is present (in fact, both). Rule is satisfied.

requirements.description: CloudFront Distribution S3 origin has OriginAccessControlId explicitly set to empty string and OriginAccessIdentity is empty/absent
requirements.rationale: An empty OriginAccessControlId does not associate any OAC with the origin. Combined with absent OAI, no access restriction is enforced.

requirements.description: CloudFront Distribution has only non-S3 origins (e.g., CustomOriginConfig pointing to HTTP servers, ELBs) and no S3OriginConfig origins at all
requirements.rationale: Per resolved decision: when there are no S3 origins, there is nothing for the rule to evaluate — no S3 origin buckets means no violation.

requirements.description: CloudFront Distribution S3 origin has OriginAccessControlId set, and the referenced AWS::CloudFront::OriginAccessControl in the same template has SigningBehavior set to 'no-override' or 'never' (not 'always')
requirements.rationale: Per resolved decision: the mere presence of OriginAccessControlId is sufficient to consider access restriction enforced. The rule does not validate the OAC's SigningBehavior value.

requirements.description: CloudFront Distribution S3 origin has OriginAccessIdentity set to any non-empty arbitrary string value (even one that is not a properly formatted OAI path)
requirements.rationale: The rule treats any non-empty OriginAccessIdentity value as an enforced restriction. Validating the string format is beyond the rule's scope; non-emptiness is the trigger for compliance.
